walkthroughs.body_html:
Individual Oral — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Individual Oral brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Individual Oral.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold
Foreshadowing is the shadow a character casts in a scene.
Subtle hints or clues earlier in a text that anticipate later events, making the resolution feel both surprising and inevitable.
Foreshadowing is when a character predicts the future.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.
A bildungsroman is a novel about constructing buildings.
A bildungsroman is a novel about constructing buildings.
Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
Any novel with a young protagonist is a bildungsroman.
A novel tracing a protagonist's moral and psychological development from youth to adulthood — typically involving formative experiences and a clearer sense of self.
